chain.label: Otay Mountain terrain immediately east of SDM
chain.trigger: The rising terrain associated with the Otay Mountain peaks begins about 2 nm east-northeast of SDM, and the highest terrain, at an elevation of 3,566 feet msl, is located about 7 nm east of SDM.

chain.label: Dark night over rural terrain with few visual cues
chain.trigger: Given that the accident flight occurred at night, over rural terrain, and with few visual cues and that the overcast cloud layer would have prevented moonlight from illuminating the terrain...

chain.label: Overcast ceiling at 2,100 feet agl over the departure area
chain.trigger: At 2353, reported conditions were winds calm, ceiling overcast at 2,100 feet agl, visibility 8 miles.

chain.label: Both pilots fatigued at the end of a long duty day
chain.trigger: At the time of the accident, the captain had been awake about 17.5 hours, the copilot had been awake about 16 hours, and both pilots had accumulated about 11 hours duty time... the copilot yawned five times within 6 minutes during the departure discussion.

chain.label: No TAWS installed and none required at the time
chain.trigger: The airplane was not equipped with a TAWS, which was not required equipment at the time of the accident but is required now for all U.S.-registered turbine-powered airplanes configured with six or more passenger seats.

chain.label: Crew unfamiliar with SDM and its terrain/departure procedures
chain.trigger: A review of the copilot's flight log revealed no record of previous flights into or out of SDM... Neither the captain nor the copilot mentioned the mountainous terrain to the east and northeast as a consideration in deciding which runway to use for departure.

chain.label: Crew obtained no weather information before departure
chain.trigger: They listened only to the remarks portion of the recording and did not listen to the weather information... The flight crewmember did not request any weather information or an IFR clearance and clearance void time.

caused_by.evidence: it is likely that physiological and psychological fatigue had adversely affected the ability of both pilots to properly plan the departure and assess the risks associated with it

chain.label: Elected to depart VFR at night without an IFR clearance
chain.trigger: After the copilot's fourth failed attempt to obtain the IFR clearance using the radio, the captain said, "all right, let's just do VFR." ... The flight crew did not attempt to obtain the IFR clearance by telephone, even though they had cellular and satellite telephones on board the airplane.

caused_by.evidence: Research has shown that fatigue can cause pilots to make risky, impulsive decisions and to become fixated on one aspect of a situation.

chain.label: Straight-out runway 8L departure instead of the published obstacle departure procedure
chain.trigger: The accident captain and copilot did not follow the recommended departure procedure and instead flew the airplane straight out on a heading toward the mountains.

caused_by.evidence: The flight crew decided to depart under VFR from runway 8L after unsuccessful attempts to obtain an IFR clearance using the communication radios.
Neither the captain nor the copilot mentioned the mountainous terrain to the east and northeast as a consideration in deciding which runway to use for departure.
fatigue had adversely affected the ability of both pilots to properly plan the departure and assess the risks associated with it

chain.label: Level at 2,300 feet msl, below the 5,000-foot MVA and surrounding peaks
chain.trigger: the airplane climbed to about 2,300 feet mean sea level (msl) and leveled out, and its flight track remained approximately straight out from the departure runway... The minimum vectoring altitude (MVA) in this area was 5,000 feet msl.

caused_by.evidence: flew the airplane straight out on a heading toward the mountains and leveled off at an altitude of 2,300 feet msl
leveled off at an altitude of 2,300 feet msl, presumably to maintain VFR below the cloud ceiling
the captain and the copilot did not listen to the weather portion of the ATIS, which reported overcast ceilings at 2,100 feet agl

chain.label: Controller vectored the VFR flight toward rising terrain below the MVA
chain.trigger: fly heading of zero two zero [degrees] maintain vfr and as soon as you get above five thousand [feet] I'll uh have an ifr clearance for ya... the heading issued by the controller resulted in a flight track that continued toward the mountains.

caused_by.evidence: the captain contacted the Southern California Terminal Radar Approach Control (SCT TRACON) controller after takeoff to pick up the flight's IFR clearance

chain.label: No safety alert issued despite MSAW alerts and known terrain
chain.trigger: the controller's computer system generated aural and visual MSAW alerts on his display, yet the controller took no action to warn the flight crew about the MSAW alerts.

caused_by.evidence: the controller's computer system issued a minimum safe altitude warning (MSAW)... during the flight's last two mode C radar returns at 0024:59 and 0025:03

The controller stated that he was aware of the mountainous terrain east SDM. When asked why he took no action to warn the flight crew of the airplane's proximity to terrain, the controller stated that it was the pilot's responsibility to avoid terrain when operating under VFR.

chain.label: Crew did not see the rising unlighted terrain ahead
chain.trigger: it is likely that the flight crew did not see the rising terrain as the airplane continued toward it

caused_by.evidence: At night, clouds and terrain are difficult for pilots to see, and a gradual loss of visual cues can occur as flight is continued toward darker terrain.
the airplane continued directly toward mountains that included terrain elevations as high as 3,566 feet msl
The purpose of a TAWS is to determine possible terrain conflicts along the airplane's flightpath and provide a warning to pilots in time for them to take corrective action.
The controller had the knowledge and opportunity to alert the flight crew to an unsafe condition, but he failed to do so.

chain.label: Controlled flight into mountainous terrain 8 nm east of SDM
chain.trigger: crashed into mountainous terrain shortly after takeoff from Brown Field Municipal Airport... The initial impact point was at an elevation of 2,256 feet msl.

caused_by.evidence: flew the airplane straight out on a heading toward the mountains
the airplane was about 4.5 nm east of SDM and was no longer climbing after having leveled off at 2,300 feet msl
it is likely that the flight crew did not see the rising terrain as the airplane continued toward it
the heading issued by the controller resulted in a flight track that allowed the airplane to continue directly toward mountains
his failure to take appropriate action placed the airplane in an unsafe situation

chain.label: Five occupants killed, airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The captain, the copilot, and the three medical crewmembers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed.

caused_by.evidence: the autopsy reports stated the cause of death for both the captain and the copilot was "blunt and sharp force injuries"
